newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek money rates hold but nervousness subsides.
newsitem.headline: Greek money rates hold but nervousness subsides.

text.p: Greek financial markets were calmer in late dealings but interest rates had stabilised around midday levels and ecu/drachma was trading slightly below the 302.690 at the fixing, dealers said.

"The market is definitely calmer now but rates have steadied at high levels," said a trader at a foreign bank. "I think this is going to last for a while as players move to cash in profits in ecu/drachma carry trades."
Dealers estimated that a total of 200 to 250 million ecus were bought by banks at the fixing with an outflow of $400 million taking placing on Monday evening.
"Many banks seek funding for next week's auction and this adds to the upward pressure on interest rates," another dealer said.
Greece will auction about 300 billion drachmas worth of seven-year FRNs and five-year fixed coupon bonds next week, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis told reporters on Monday.
A finance ministry statement said 100 billion drachmas of five-year fixed coupon bonds, the first ever, will be auctioned.
The mark was quoted at 158.40/50 drachmas from Tuesday's 158.260 fix, the dollar at 237.37/47 drachmas from 236.700 and the Ecu at 302.68/78 from 302.690 drachmas.
